## SECT. II. _Of the Formation of Shells._

THE hell or covering of teffaceous animals, has been considered as in fome measure analogous to the bones of other animals, although its formation and growth are very different, since it ferves as a bafe or support to the muteles, which are attached to its inter- nal surface. The principal ufe of the hell, however, is to ferve as a covering or defence to the animal.

Teltaccous animals are not only extremely different in external form, but alfo in the mode of their production. Some are viviparous, as the moft of thofe which inhabit bivalve hells, multivalves, and even fome of the univalves; while the others, which form the far greater proportion, are oviparous. In one point, how ever, they all agree, that whatever be the mode of production, whether from an egg, or directly from the uterus of the mother, the hell is formed on the body of the young animal, and is proportioned to its bulk.
